checks: The Hausdorff assumption gives h_K(u)≥h_T(u)−δ||u||₁, and T₋+[−δ,δ]^m⊂T because the perturbation changes each coordinate by at most δ and the sum by at most mδ. Support comparison gives T₋⊂K. Matching a K-point to a T-point within δ gives K⊂T₊. These are translates of (1−2mδ)T and (1+2mδ)T respectively, with positive scales. The outer simplex is feasible, so each minimizer satisfies the volume bound.

For δ=0 one has K=T. Any extra point in S violates a facet inequality of T and gives a positive-volume cone on that facet outside T, contradicting |S|≤|T|. Thus S=T and the vertex and centroid estimates hold with error zero.

For δ>0 put L=1−2mδ. Each coordinate facet of T₋ has area L^(m−1)/(m−1)!, and the top facet has √m times that area. Perpendicular height for the top facet divides its inequality deficit by √m. The volume of each violated-facet cone is therefore L^(m−1)|T| times its positive deficit. The cone lies in S by convexity and meets T₋ only on the facet, so its volume is bounded by |S|−|T₋|. The argument works for any convex body S under the volume cap; no cones for different facets are added. For m=1 the facet is a point and the cone length is exactly the deficit.

With a=2mδ≤1/(4m), the odd-binomial numerator of Δ is at least 2ma=4m²δ and its denominator at most one. By the mean-value theorem the numerator is at most 2ma(1+a)^(m−1); Bernoulli and termwise domination by the geometric series of ratio (m−1)a give a ratio of at most (4/3)/(3/4)=16/9<2. Hence 4m²δ≤Δ≤8m²δ and E=Δ−δ≥mδ since 4m²−1≥m. The top bound 1−mδ+Δ≤1+E holds for m≥1.

The facet bounds give S⊂−E1+[1+(m+1)E]T. Under this map each displacement coordinate is E((m+1)t_i−1)∈[−E,mE]. In the reverse direction each point of T is within δ of K⊂S. Since δ≤mE, the Hausdorff error is at most mE≤8m³δ.

The maximum of coordinate i over S occurs at a vertex, and approximation of e_i gives value at least 1−δ. The sum bound and other lower coordinate bounds give x_i≤1+mE and x_j≤δ+(m−1)E≤mE for j≠i. A vertex minimizing the sum has sum at most mδ by approximation of zero, hence each coordinate is at most mδ+(m−1)E≤mE. The radii mE≤1/8 give pairwise disjoint neighborhoods since the reference vertices have pairwise infinity distance one. The chosen m+1 vertices exhaust the simplex. Averaging matched vertices opposite each label retains the same error bound; the predecessor supplies membership in K.
